text:
sam: Heads up — saw a p99 regression on the continuous-batcher rollout after the new prefix-cache packing landed.

sam: Numbers from main cluster vs last week: p50 ~42ms (same), p95 120ms -> 170ms, p99 230ms -> 410ms, tokens/sec per-GPU down ~18%. KV cache hit ratio actually went up (was ~58% -> 76%), which made this surprising. :thinking:

jin: interesting. do we have kernel-switch counts and packing efficiency metrics? sounds like we might be oscillating kernels due to smaller effective token lengths on cache hits.

sam: yep — I pulled a flamegraph and a short perf trace. two quick observations: kernel-switch-per-batch spikes (we see more short-run kernels chosen) and "wasted_slots_percent" increases because many batches become thin after applying prefix cache.

sam: snippet from the perf trace (simplified):
```
# batch_id, kernel_chosen, batch_effective_tokens, cuda_time_ms
12345, kern_a_short, 60, 4.2
12346, kern_b_long, 420, 23.7
12347, kern_a_short, 58, 4.0
12348, kern_b_long, 430, 24.1
# switching causes extra memcpy/ll_cache steps and scheduling overhead
```

anya: hypothesis: cache-hits reduce the runtime token budget per request, which reduces the observed sequence length distribution the packer sees. packer then forms "dense" batches of mixed lengths that favor short-kernel choices and cause bouncing. two levers to consider: (1) change batching "virtual length" for cache-hit items (treat them as if longer for packing purposes only), (2) add a small coalesce delay for cache-hit traffic so we can fill batches more predictably.

jin: both sound plausible. we should be careful not to inflate measured token usage (billing) — this is internal packing metadata only. can you draft the config we'd need to try?

anya: quick experiment config (safe, server-side only):
```json
{
  "batching": {
    "token_budget_target": 1024,
    "max_pack_delay_ms": 6,
    "cache_hit_virtual_factor": 1.8,
    "min_virtual_length": 32
  }
}
```
Explanation: cache_hit_virtual_factor multiplies the observed runtime tokens for packing decisions only. min_virtual_length prevents extremely short cache hits from collapsing batch formation. max_pack_delay_ms is low to bound added latency.

raj: sounds good. what metrics do we track in the canary? I'd add: kernel_switches_per_minute, packing_efficiency (actual_tokens_sent / theoretical_capacity), wasted_slots_percent, p50/p95/p99 latency, and end-to-end tokens/sec. also track tail latency for cold requests (no cache).

sam: agreed. I'll run a canary at 5% on a Dedicated pool and generate synthetic traces that replicate the real prefix-cache hit distribution. command I'm using to replay:
```bash
./bench_client --trace-file traces/prefix-heavy.json --rps 120 --target-pool dedicated-a --collect-metrics
```

perf-bot: Canary started on pool dedicated-a (5%). Initial synthetic run (10m) results: kernel_switches_per_min 420 -> 90 (down), packing_efficiency 0.64 -> 0.83, p99 410ms -> 195ms. No errors observed. :tada:

jin: interesting improvement on the synthetic run. what's the impact on average GPU utilization?

perf-bot: GPU utilization increased ~12% on the canary hosts; tokens/sec recovered to within 4% of baseline.

anya: nice. still want to validate on real traffic because the synthetic run doesn't capture some burstiness. propose A/B for 48h on 10% traffic, then revert if p99 > baseline + 10% or error rate jumps.

raj: and let's add a safeguard: if kernel_switches_per_min spikes > 2x during the canary, auto-revert. we don't want pathological cases where virtualizing length causes bad long-kernel selection for genuinely short requests.

sam: implemented the canary config and the rollback rule. kicking off 48h. will post results here. :memo:

perf-bot: Canary metrics will be posted to /reports/eng-runtime/canary_1988880000.json every 15m.

sam: thanks — if anyone wants to look at the raw traces I uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/traces/1988880000-prefix-virtuality, ping me.

jin: good thread. if this works we should consider making the cache_hit_virtual_factor adaptive (learn from kernel-switch counts). but first get the safety net in. :eyes:
